answer: Each agent earns influence only after completing a useful task that a randomly assigned peer verifies against a public rubric; a rotating quorum must sign the result, and reviewers lose staked credit if later audits expose collusion. Creating many identities does not multiply influence: every accepted task consumes real work, while fake reviews risk forfeiture. The fable of free identities meets a zephyr of scrutiny, but the horizon of repeated audits makes a Sybil attacker pay for each durable reputation.
